newsitem.title: USA: Electricidade de Portugal stock soars in U.S. trading.
newsitem.headline: Electricidade de Portugal stock soars in U.S. trading.

text.p: The stock of Portugal's national electric company, Electricidade de Portugal, shot up more than 33 percent in its first day of U.S. trading Tuesday.
EDP's stock rose $8.65625 to $34.50 in heavy trading on the New York Stock Exchange. where it was the the biggest percentage gainer, on volume of more than 3.6 million shares.
The Portuguese government sold a 30 percent stake in a first-stage privatisation of EDP-Electricidade, the largest company yet to be partially privatised in Portugal.
The global offering of 179 million shares, which was sold Monday, was worth more than $2 billion. The shares were priced at $25.84 per share.
The underwriter, Goldman Sachs, said 23.5 million shares were sold in the United States.
The buying frenzy also sent overall trade on the Lisbon stock exchange rocketing to 65 billion escudos ($340 million), more than double the previous record high.
"EDP was the star. It was a really brilliant day," said one trader in Lisbon.
Analysts said that one of the surprising aspects of the trading activity was the huge interest of the small investor in Portugal.

"The most surprising thing about EDP was the buying that came from the retail (small investor). This did not happen at the previous privatisations," said Jose Freire, an analyst for Espirito Santo Research.
Electricidade de Portugal Deputy Chairman Arnaldo Navcarro Machado said the company is looking for additional overseas investments.
He said in an interview that the company has already acquired 21 percent of Brazil's Companhia de Eletricidade do Rio de Janeiro SA and has been managing the company since late last year.
The cash raised by the company's stock offering will go to the government, he said, adding that the offering was "more successful ... than everybody thought" it would be.
The company is interested in investing in South America, and North Africa, Machado said, citing Brazil and Morocco specifically as "countries where we feel comfortable."
He said EDP is "looking for other opportunities" in Brazil, where it invested with Spanish and Chilean companies.
In Portugal, Machado said, power demand is expected to grow faster than the nation's gross domestic product, which is forecast to increase 3.5 percent per year through 2000.
EDP Executive Director Jorge Cruz Morais said the company's present capacity is about half hydropower and half fossil fuel -- coal and fuel oil.
He said EDP has a 30 percent stake in a pipeline that will import natural gas from Algeria via Gibraltar and Seville, Spain. The line continues through Portugal to Leon, Spain.
